states.edition: Nebraska State Building Code — 2018 International Residential Code, except section R313 and chapters 25–33 (Neb. Rev. Stat. 71-6403)
states.differs_from_app: Edition matches. 'Since' should be 2019: LB 348 (approved by the Governor April 17, 2019) moved the IRC reference from the 2012 to the 2018 edition; the bill has no emergency clause and its operative date was not confirmed. Also, the state does not inspect homes itself: a county/city/village that enforces a code must adopt the state code or one that 'conforms generally' (a newer edition counts, e.g. Lincoln is on the 2021 IRC), and must update within two years of a state update (71-6406).
notes: Section R313 (residential fire sprinklers) and chapters 25–33 (plumbing) are excluded from the state adoption.
No state amendments to guards, stairs or decks — IRC values apply unless the local code changes them (Lincoln allows 5 in. guard openings).
LB 1134 (2026 session) would keep the 2018 IRC as the state edition; its status was not confirmed.

counties.edition: 2024 IRC with Independence amendments (effective January 1, 2025); unincorporated Jackson County enforces the 2018 IRC (County Code Ch. 54)
counties.wind_basis: 115 mph as listed in Independence's 2024 IRC amendment to Table R301.2(1); the amendment does not say whether this is Vult or Vasd. Topographic effects No, special wind region No, windborne debris zone No.
deck_notes: Independence's 2024 IRC amendments delete R105.2 Building item 10, which in the IRC is the small freestanding deck exemption, so small decks are not exempt in Independence.
Independence deck permits need the residential permit application, a Deck Plan Review Sheet, a Covered Deck sheet if roofed, an expanded deck detail and a plot plan.
Independence deck footings must be at least 36 inches deep and at least twice the post size in width or diameter.
Independence limits openings between spindles and the rail gap to 3-7/8 inches, stair rise to 7-3/4 inches, and requires stair run of at least 10 inches.
Independence's packet requires a handrail 34 to 38 inches high on stairs with 3 or more risers.
Independence's review sheet says beams must be notched and bolted through support posts, and the rim joist must be bolted through rail posts; ledgers use 1/2-inch lag screws or bolts.
Independence reviews deck permits within 5 business days through Building, Zoning (setbacks) and Engineering (easements and floodplains).
In unincorporated Jackson County, decks that do not exceed 36 inches above grade are exempt from a building permit (Ch. 54).

An unincorporated Jackson County deck permit needs a legal description, 2 copies of a site plan (property and structure dimensions, setbacks on all 4 sides, north arrow, streams, septic), 2 sets of drawings with lumber sizes and spacing, and the square footage and valuation.
counties.note: Unincorporated Jackson County publishes no filled-in Table R301.2(1) (its Ch. 54 adopts the 2018 I-codes without climatic values), so the climatic values are Independence's. The posted Independence amendment PDF is the unsigned council bill (dated 11/15/24, effective Jan 1, 2025), listed by the city as its adopted 2024 IRC amendments; the city's deck packet also cites the 2024 IRC. Kansas City, MO values could not be verified (kcmo.gov and Municode returned 403). Independence also lists winter design temp 6 F, ice barrier Yes, AFI 927 and MAT 55.5 F.

counties.jurisdiction: Johnson County Planning, Housing and Community Development - Building Codes Division (unincorporated Johnson County only; cities such as Overland Park and Olathe run their own departments)
counties.edition: 2018 IRC with amendments in the Johnson County Code of Regulations for Buildings and Construction, 2018 Edition (effective July 1, 2020); the 2024 I-codes are up for adoption on Oct 22, 2026, effective Jan 1, 2027 if adopted
counties.wind_basis: 115 mph as printed in the county's amended 2018 IRC Table R301.2(1) (not labeled Vult or Vasd); topographic effects No, special wind region No, windborne debris zone No. The draft 2024 table keeps 115 mph, and its footnote d cites the 'ultimate design wind speeds map [Figure R301.2(2)]'.
deck_notes: The county permits page says all decks require a permit, including deck repairs; however, the county's posted exemption list repeats the IRC exemption for freestanding decks of 200 sq ft or less, no more than 30 inches above grade, and not serving the required exit door.
Submit a scaled site plan with lot dimensions, easements, building lines and distances to property lines (setbacks); the builder or homeowner may draw it, with no seal required.
Submit a scaled deck plan showing decking, joist size and spacing, beams, posts, pier sizes and depth, and ledger attachment; no seal is needed for decks built within the guideline.

Piers must be at least 36 inches deep (below frost), with the top at least 1 inch above grade and sloped for drainage; pier diameter depends on the deck area each pier supports (for example 12 in. for 24 sq ft, 14 in. for 32 sq ft, at 1,500 psf soil).
The guideline covers only 40 psf live and 10 psf dead load; multi-level decks, roofs, hot tubs, spas and over-limit cantilevers need specific approval or a design professional.

Ledgers must be lagged or bolted to the house rim joist (never nailed) with double flashing and hot-dip galvanized or stainless fasteners, and may not be attached to or through brick, stone, stucco or masonry veneer; build a freestanding deck instead.
Posts need a column anchor that resists uplift and lateral movement (e.g., Simpson AB66R); a drift pin alone is not enough.
Freestanding decks more than 2 feet above grade need diagonal bracing or attachment to the house for lateral load.
Guards at least 36 inches high are required where the deck floor is more than 30 inches above grade within 36 inches horizontally of the edge.
An exterior light for the deck and stair lighting are required, and overhead power lines must be at least 10 ft above the deck floor or 3 ft away horizontally.
The draft 2024 county code amends R507.1 so that decks built to the Johnson County Residential Deck Guidelines are deemed approved.
counties.note: The deck guide ('Residential Decks Permit and Construction Guidelines under the 2018 IRC', 4th ed., Jan 2019) is endorsed by the Johnson County Building Officials Association for use across Johnson County jurisdictions, so Overland Park and other cities' rules are likely similar; Overland Park's own site was not readable (JavaScript-rendered) and was not checked. Code change pending: on Oct 22, 2026 (two days from now) the Board of County Commissioners will consider the 2024 I-codes, effective Jan 1, 2027 if adopted. The draft 2024 table keeps snow 20, wind 115, SDC A, Severe, frost 36 in., termite M-H, and changes AFI from 927 to 1000. Other 2018 table values: winter design temp 6 F, ice barrier Yes, flood Aug. 2009, MAT 55 F.

Attached decks must be positively anchored for vertical and lateral loads, without toenails or nails in withdrawal; if the connection can't be verified at inspection the deck must be self-supporting.
Cantilevered deck framing connections must resist uplift from the full live load on the cantilever.
Footings must go below the 24-inch frost line ('Frost depth in Wichita is 24 inches'), and footings may not bear on frozen soil.
The amended table lists a 40 psf live load and 10 psf dead load for floors.
Permit staff check site plans for FEMA flood soils, easements and rights-of-way.
Residential permit fees for decks are $0.30 per square foot.
counties.note: Unusual: the MABCD table's wind entry uses an older basic-wind format (76/90 mph), and its 15 psf snow and 24-inch frost are lower than the Kansas City area. MABCD lists 2018 IRC as current even though the IBC and IEBC moved to 2024 (Resolutions 205-2024 / 203-2024). The 'City of Wichita Standard for Residential Wood Framed Decks' is referenced but was not located. counties.jurisdiction: Lincoln-Lancaster County Planning & Development Services, Building & Safety (City of Lincoln and its 3-mile area; serves Lancaster County residents)
counties.edition: 2021 IRC (2nd printing) with Lincoln amendments — Lincoln Municipal Code ch. 20.12 (Ord. 21820, Dec 15, 2025; earlier Ord. 20937, June 29, 2020)
counties.wind_basis: Lincoln amended Table R301.2 (2021 IRC, ultimate design wind speed per footnote d)
deck_notes: All new and replacement decks require a building permit; Lincoln's exempt-work list (LMC 20.12.035) has no deck exemption.
The permit needs a site plan with lot dimensions and setback distances from the deck to the property lines, plus how the deck will be built.
Attached decks must bear on the house and/or frost-free footings at least 36 in. deep; freestanding decks under 400 sq ft not supported by a dwelling may skip frost footings (LMC 20.12.445).
Guards at least 36 in. high are required where the deck is more than 30 in. above grade, and also where there is a drop of more than 30 in. within 60 in. of the walking-surface edge (LMC 20.12.355).
Lincoln allows guard openings up to a 5 in. sphere (LMC 20.12.360), not the IRC's 4 in.
Stair risers 4 in. minimum and 7¾ in. maximum; treads 10 in. minimum; handrail on at least one side when there are more than three risers.
Posts must sit on top of and be connected to the footing (manufactured connectors for lateral restraint), never buried in the ground or footing.
Joists may cantilever no more than 24 in. past the beam and beams no more than 16 in. past the post; a hot tub adds 50 psf to the design load.
Lateral load: at least two 1,500 lb hold-down devices within 24 in. of each end of the deck, or four 750 lb devices (LMC 20.12.595).
counties.note: Values are the Lincoln Municipal Code 20.12.140 Table R301.2 (as amended Dec 15, 2025): ground snow 25 psf, wind 115 mph, SDC B, severe weathering, frost 36 in., termite moderate to heavy, winter design temp printed as '70° F' (looks like a typo in the code), ice barrier yes. Lincoln uses a newer IRC edition than the 2018 state code, which Neb. Rev. Stat. 71-6406 permits. Deck brochure updated 2/23/2026; deck detail drawing dated 27 March 2026.

counties.jurisdiction: City of Sioux Falls Planning & Development Services, Building Services (county seat and largest city)
counties.edition: 2024 IRC with Sioux Falls local amendments (Code of Ordinances §150.001; effective July 1, 2026, applied to permits issued after Oct 15, 2026)
counties.wind_basis: Ultimate design wind speed from Figure R301.2(2) (2024 IRC table footnote d)
deck_notes: Sioux Falls removes the IRC permit exemption for small, low, detached decks (its R105.2 item 10 covers only window, door and siding work), so decks need a permit.
Decks not supported by a dwelling need not have footings below the frost line (R507.3 exception as amended).
A deck projection less than 3 ft from a common property line needs a 1-hour fire-rated wall, rated from both sides with no openings, extending at least 30 in. above the deck (R302.1 as amended).
Exterior stairs to grade with three or fewer risers serving a deck may have a 36 in. wide bottom landing if they are not the required egress route.
Sioux Falls amends stairs to allow risers up to 8 in. (R318.7.5.1) and guards with openings up to a 5 in. sphere (R321.1.3); treads stay at the IRC 10 in.
Handrails are required on flights with four or more risers, except where the total rise is 30 in. or less.

counties.jurisdiction: City of Fargo Inspections Department (county seat and largest city; Cass County itself is not on the state's list of code-enforcing jurisdictions — West Fargo and Casselton enforce their own)
counties.edition: 2024 IRC with Fargo local amendment (in effect in Fargo as of July 2, 2025)
deck_notes: Every new or replacement patio deck needs a building permit in Fargo.
Fargo does not require footings for uncovered decks attached to the house to go below the 4½-ft frost depth, but encourages it; freestanding decks should have footings at least 12 in. below grade.
A deck designed or engineered for a future enclosure needs frost footings and a foundation inspection.
The permit plan must show the size and location of posts, beams and stairs, drawn to scale or fully dimensioned so spans and cantilevers can be checked.

Ledgers must be at least 2x8 pressure-treated, fastened with two staggered rows of ½ in. hot-dipped galvanized or stainless lags or bolts, flashed, and may not attach to cantilevered floors or bay windows.
Beam and joist cantilevers are limited to one quarter of the adjacent span.
Inspections: framing (before decking goes on) and final; a flat 2x4 or 2x6 is not accepted as a handrail.
Guards at least 36 in. high are required where the deck is more than 30 in. above grade.
counties.note: Fargo publishes no Table R301.2 values online that I could find; the 4½-ft (54 in.) frost depth is stated in the city's Patio Decks handout (revised 10/2/2019, written for an earlier IRC). Snow, wind, seismic, weathering and termite left null. The ND state amendment for the 2024 IRC (R507.3 exception) also lets decks not supported by a frost-protected structure skip frost footings. Fargo's current-codes page links its 2024 IRC local amendment on Municode, which I could not open (bot wall).

counties.jurisdiction: Pikes Peak Regional Building Department (PPRBD) — Colorado Springs and unincorporated El Paso County (plus member towns)
counties.edition: 2023 Pikes Peak Regional Building Code (2nd printing 6/30/2026), adopting the 2021 IRC with regional amendments (RBC303)
counties.wind_basis: Ultimate design wind speed Vult per ASCE 7-16, Exposure C minimum (PPRBC Table R301.2; Risk Cat. I/II; 135 Cat. III, 140 Cat. IV)
deck_notes: Detached decks of 200 sq ft or less, no more than 30 in. above grade within 36 in. of the deck edge and not serving the required egress door, need no permit (RBC105.2.1 item 9).
Foundation drawings must normally be sealed by a Colorado-licensed engineer, but decks set on unreinforced concrete piers are exempt from that (R401.1.1 exception 3).
Detached, uncovered decks with a walking surface no more than 24 in. above grade may sit directly on grade instead of frost footings (R403.1.4.1 exception 2).
Decks are designed for the floor live load of R301.5; R507.1 is amended so the deck snow load is not used.
Ledger must be at least a 2x8, may not hang on stone or masonry veneer, and may not attach to an unsupported rim without an engineered connection (R507.9 as amended).
IRC R507.10 (exterior guards) is deleted, so deck guards follow the general guard rules of R312.
counties.note: Snow load is set by elevation of the grade plane: below 7,000 ft pg = 43 psf (flat roof pf = 30 psf); at or above 7,000 ft pg = 57 psf (pf = 40 psf). Colorado Springs is below 7,000 ft, so 43 psf ground / 30 psf roof. PPRBD's Basic Design Information sheet (updated 06/30/2026) lists Ss 18.5%, S1 5.9%. Frost depth, SDC, weathering and termite are from the PPRBC Table R301.2. The regional code is still on the 2021 IRC as of the 2nd printing dated 6/30/2026.

counties.jurisdiction: City and County of Denver, Community Planning & Development (Denver Residential Code)
counties.edition: 2025 Denver Building and Fire Code — 2025 Denver Residential Code based on the 2024 IRC (adopted June 13, 2025; city page: effective December 31; 2nd-printing updates adopted Nov 24, 2025)
counties.wind_basis: Table R301.2 lists 115/125/140 mph (ultimate design wind speeds by risk category, 2024 IRC/ASCE 7-22 basis); 115 is the Risk Category II value used for dwellings
deck_notes: Uncovered decks (with their guards, stairs and ramps) of 200 sq ft or less with walking surfaces no more than 30 in. above grade need no building permit.
Uncovered decks more than 12 in. off the ground need a zoning permit, and decks 30 in. or more off the ground also need a building permit; covered decks need both.
The site plan must be drawn to scale with a scale and north arrow, dimensioned zone lot lines, streets/alleys, existing structures, and distances from the new deck to structures and lot lines.

Plans must show beam and joist sizes and spans, post size, footing size and depth, ledger connection, uplift connection, roll blocking at cantilevers, decking, stair, guard and handrail details, and cantilever lengths.
Where a built-in bench or similar raised surface abuts an open side more than 72 in. above grade, the 36 in. guard is measured from the top of that raised surface (Denver amendment to R321.1.2).
counties.note: Ground snow 43 psf is the allowable-stress (pg(asd)) worst case within city limits (was 35 psf before the 2025 code); a new footnote allows a location-specific value from the ASCE 7 Hazard Tool (Risk Category II). The Residential Decks web page gives no frost depth; 36 in. comes from the Denver Residential Code Table R301.2. The 'effective December 31' date on the city page has no year shown; the adoption was June 13, 2025.

A Colorado-licensed engineer's stamp may be required for roof-covered decks, designs outside the IRC tables, and decks carrying hot tubs, spas or planters.
